item.text:
**4B.8 Research Note**

Overall judgment: **Mixed, leaning no**. Sharif did follow the formal parliamentary transfer path and did not show an obvious term-limit violation, but the 2024 election and succession environment was heavily disputed, and the main opposition was structurally disadvantaged. Coalition bargaining was real, and he did not obviously break the coalition format, but the process was not clean enough to support a positive ruling.

- [Shehbaz Sharif to be coalition candidate for next Pakistan PM -spokeswoman](https://theprint.in/world/shehbaz-sharif-to-be-coalition-candidate-for-next-pakistan-pm-spokeswoman/1965379/) - **Reuters**, 2024-02-14. Claim: After a hung parliament, PPP said it would support Sharif to form a minority government, and Sharif became the coalition candidate. This is the strongest positive item for respecting constitutional succession and coalition formation, because the government was assembled through parliamentary bargaining rather than a unilateral seizure. **QIDs:** 4B.8, 4B.2, 4B.1.

- [Pakistan’s largest parties strike deal on coalition government](https://theprint.in/world/pakistans-largest-parties-strike-deal-on-coalition-government/1973213/) - **Reuters**, 2024-02-21. Claim: PML-N and PPP reached a formal agreement to form a coalition government, ending negotiations after the hung election. This supports a reading that Sharif accepted coalition government rules and did not reject transfer procedures. **QIDs:** 4B.8, 4B.2.

- [Pakistan’s newly elected assembly meets amid pro-Imran Khan protests](https://www.streetinsider.com/Reuters/Pakistan%27s%2Bnewly%2Belected%2Bassembly%2Bmeets%2Bamid%2Bpro-Imran%2BKhan%2Bprotests/22856039.html) - **Reuters**, 2024-02-29. Claim: The new assembly met by the constitutional deadline, with PTI-backed independents alleging the election was rigged while PML-N and PPP moved to form a coalition. This shows the constitutional transfer machinery still operated, but under acute legitimacy dispute. **QIDs:** 4B.8, 4B.1, 4B.2.

- [Shehbaz Sharif elected Pakistan’s prime minister for second term](https://theprint.in/india/shehbaz-sharif-elected-pakistans-prime-minister-for-second-term/1986782/) - **Reuters**, 2024-03-03. Claim: Parliament formally elected Sharif prime minister for a second term, and he had returned to the role he held until August 2023 when parliament was dissolved. This is direct positive evidence that he did not ignore succession rules or overstay a term. **QIDs:** 4B.8, 4B.1.

- [Pakistan’s Shehbaz Sharif takes oath as prime minister, directs team to talk with IMF](https://www.investing.com/news/economy/pakistans-shehbaz-sharif-takes-oath-as-prime-minister-3322834) - **Reuters**, 2024-03-04. Claim: Sharif was sworn in after the election and took office through the normal parliamentary route, following a caretaker period. This supports constitutional transfer of power, though it does not resolve the election’s contested legitimacy. **QIDs:** 4B.8, 4B.1.

- [Pakistan’s Imran Khan’s party loses cricket bat electoral symbol](https://theprint.in/world/pakistans-imran-khans-party-loses-cricket-bat-electoral-symbol/1923216/) - **Reuters**, 2024-01-14. Claim: The Election Commission and Supreme Court removed PTI’s bat symbol on technical intra-party-election grounds, materially disadvantaging Sharif’s main opponent before the vote. That is negative evidence against respecting fair succession rules and against clean competitive transfer. **QIDs:** 4B.8, 4B.2, 4B.1.

- [US, UK and EU urge probe into Pakistan election, express concerns](https://www.theprint.in/world/us-uk-eu-urge-probe-into-pakistan-election-express-concerns/1961577/) - **Reuters**, 2024-02-10. Claim: Major external partners expressed concerns about interference, irregularities, and fraud and urged a probe. This is strong counterevidence that the 2024 succession process was fully legitimate or clean. **QIDs:** 4B.8, 4B.1, 4B.2.

- [US concerned about reports of intimidation, voter suppression in Pakistan election, White House says](https://www.investing.com/news/world-news/us-concerned-about-reports-of-intimidation-voter-suppression-in-pakistan-election-white-house-says-3305341) - **Reuters**, 2024-02-15. Claim: The White House explicitly raised intimidation and voter-suppression concerns. This is direct negative evidence against a clean constitutional transfer grounded in unmanipulated succession rules. **QIDs:** 4B.8, 4B.1, 4B.2.

- [All’s well after PPP, PML-N settle differences](https://www.dawn.com/news/amp/1840944) - **Dawn**, 2024-06-21. Claim: PPP and PML-N resolved budget differences through dialogue, and the government formed a committee to keep taking the issue forward. This is mild positive evidence that coalition commitments were being managed through bargaining rather than open rupture. **QIDs:** 4B.8, 4B.4.

**Search gap**

- I found **no strong evidence** that Sharif violated a formal term limit or attempted an unconstitutional extension of his mandate.
- The stronger issue is that the **electoral succession environment was contested and arguably manipulated**, especially via PTI’s symbol loss, election irregularities concerns, and voter-suppression allegations.
- So the cleanest reading is: **formal transfer yes, clean respect for constitutional succession norms no**.
